title: Tesla's self-driving system misreads speed limits, safety group says
key_facts: Belgian nonprofit Johanna.be tested a Tesla Model 3 over three days in July, about 400 km, running FSD 14.2.2.6 in Standard mode.
FSD exceeded the 30 km/h limit on 16 of 29 Brussels road segments, averaging 44 km/h at the top speed of those segments.
The car showed a wrong, higher limit to the driver on roughly 90 percent of tested segments.
It exceeded the 20 km/h limit in 5 of 12 residential home zones and repeatedly tried to pass cyclists on cycle streets.
The report says FSD generally yielded to pedestrians and cyclists.
Dutch regulator RDW approved FSD in April and told Reuters it received the report and would assess it; Tesla did not respond to Reuters.
Test was one car, one software version, selected Belgian roads.
quote_evidence: Importantly, the test involved just one car, one software version, and selected Belgian roads, so it can’t really establish how often every FSD-equipped Tesla behaves this way.
Johanna.be has asked both authorities to revisit the approvals ahead of a possible October 6 vote on use across the EU.
why_it_matters_hint: A single-car study that gives regulators specific faults to examine ahead of an EU decision.
